entries.subject: Porter 2025 single-triaxial Kerberos interpretation
entries.finding: Presentation slide 7 refines the rounded abstract to full axes 14.5 × 8.2 × 7.2 km. The package retains this approximate ellipsoid without inferred local terrain; the source does not converge on a unique pole.

entries.subject: Porter 2025 contact-binary alternative and numerical mesh
entries.finding: Slide 8 compares a contact-binary interpretation, but the retained review located no unique bilobate vertex/facet release or converged pole. No screenshot-traced mesh is substituted.
entries.revisitWhen: A numerical Kerberos solution and its uncertainty, pole and coordinate conventions are released.

entries.subject: LORRI lor_0299153805 and lor_0299136735
entries.finding: The 2026-09-08 survey decoded and inspected both original calibrated FITS frames at native pixels: approximately 1.964 and 3.127 km/pixel, only a handful of independent samples across Kerberos. They constrain shape and integrated brightness but do not provide a registered surface albedo map.
entries.revisitWhen: Resolved surface information and a controlled pose permit a meaningful cartographic footprint for Kerberos.

entries.subject: NASA PIA20034 deconvolved portrait
entries.finding: The source account identifies interlacing, deconvolution and cosmetic enlargement described by the Science supplement. This portrait is observational context, not added independent surface samples or a camera solution.
entries.revisitWhen: The underlying native images and independent registration support an observational texture.

entries.subject: Porter and Canup 2023 dimensions
entries.finding: The older approximate 19 × 10 × 9 km dimensions are superseded in this package by the explicitly approximate 2025 triaxial fit; the 2023 discussion still explains the two low-resolution viewing epochs.
entries.revisitWhen: A source comparison overturns the selected 2025 dimensions or requires displaying a separately qualified historical model.

entries.subject: MVIC, LEISA, HST and mapping-product source review
entries.finding: The retained flyby-literature and PDS survey qualified no registered color, spectral, topographic or geological Kerberos map. Disk-integrated measurements are not spatial textures, and this review does not establish that other observations do not exist.
entries.revisitWhen: A target-specific spatial product is located with adequate native information and controlled coordinates.
